Let $p\colon\mathcal S\to(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ be a category fibred in
groupoids ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]) over the fppf site
([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]). For a morphism $T'\to T$ of $S$-schemes
and an object $x$ of $\mathcal S$ over $T$ we write $x|_{T'}$ for the value of
a chosen pullback along $T'\to T$; different choices are canonically
isomorphic and the definitions below do not depend on them.

For an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ write
$T_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$ and $T_{ijk}=T_i\times_TT_j\times_TT_k$
([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). **Descent data** for a
family of objects $x_i$ of $\mathcal S_{T_i}$ is a family of isomorphisms
$$\varphi_{ij}\colon x_i|_{T_{ij}}\longrightarrow x_j|_{T_{ij}}$$
in $\mathcal S_{T_{ij}}$, one for each ordered pair $(i,j)$, satisfying the
**cocycle condition** $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ over
$T_{ijk}$ (after pulling back along the three projections and using the
canonical identifications). With the evident notion of morphism — a family of
morphisms $x_i\to y_i$ compatible with the $\varphi_{ij}$ — these data form a
category $\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\},(x_i))$, and there is a base-change functor
$\mathcal S_T\to\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\})$ sending $x$ to
$(x|_{T_i},\text{canonical isomorphisms})$.

The fibred category $\mathcal S$ is a **prestack** when for all objects $x,y$
of $\mathcal S_T$ the presheaf
$$(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}\to\mathrm{Set},\qquad U\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal S_U}(x|_U,y|_U)$$
is an fppf sheaf ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]); equivalently, for
every fppf covering the diagram of morphism sets is an equalizer.

The fibred category $\mathcal S$ is a **stack in groupoids** when it is a
prestack and every descent datum of objects is **effective**: for every fppf
covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ the base-change functor
$\mathcal S_T\to\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\})$ is an equivalence of categories.
Effectivity is thus the precise sense in which objects are glued from
descent data.

A presheaf of sets $F$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ determines a category
fibred in groupoids $\mathcal S_F$ whose fibre category over $T$ is the
**discrete groupoid** on the set $F(T)$ (the groupoid with only identity
morphisms). Descent data for $\mathcal S_F$ over a covering
$\{T_i\to T\}$ amount to a family of elements of the $F(T_i)$ whose
pullbacks agree on all $T_{ij}$, and effectivity amounts to gluing them to an
element of $F(T)$; consequently $\mathcal S_F$ is a stack in groupoids (a
**stack in setoids**) exactly when $F$ is an fppf sheaf. In particular, assuming the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in
[[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]], every
$S$-scheme $X$, whose represented presheaf is then an fppf sheaf, determines the
stack in groupoids $\mathcal S_X$ whose fibre category over $T$ is the
discrete groupoid on $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,X)$; this is the Yoneda
embedding of schemes into stacks.

An **algebraic stack** (or **Artin stack**) over $S$ is a stack in groupoids
$\mathcal X$ over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$
([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]],
[[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]) such that

1. the diagonal 1-morphism
   $\Delta\colon\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is representable by
   algebraic spaces ([[def-morphism-representable-by-algebraic-spaces]]), and
2. there exist an $S$-scheme $U$ and a 1-morphism
   $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ from the stack in setoids of $U$ which is
   representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth
   ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]).

Such a pair $(U,\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X)$ is called a **presentation** of
$\mathcal X$. The algebraic stack is **Deligne-Mumford** when a presentation
with $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ etale
([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]) can be chosen. Under the inherited Axiom of
Choice for represented-sheaf descent ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]), a scheme, viewed as a stack
in setoids, is an algebraic stack with its
identity as presentation. An algebraic space is an algebraic stack using
any of its etale scheme covers as presentation; the identity is not a
scheme presentation when the algebraic space is not a scheme.

The **inertia stack** $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}$ is the category fibred in
groupoids whose fibre category over $T$ has as objects the pairs
$(x,\alpha)$ with $x$ an object of $\mathcal X_T$ and
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X_T}(x)$. For $f:T'\to T$, a morphism from $(y,\beta)$ over $T'$ to $(x,\alpha)$ over $T$ is an arrow $\gamma:y\to x$ of $\mathcal X$ over $f$ satisfying $\gamma\beta=\alpha\gamma$. Equivalently it is a vertical isomorphism $y\to f^*x$ intertwining $\beta$ with $f^*\alpha$. Composition is composition of these arrows; cartesian uniqueness supplies the pullback identifications. The **projection**
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$, $(x,\alpha)\mapsto x$, is a
1-morphism over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.

For a 1-morphism $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of stacks in groupoids, the
**relative inertia** $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ imposes the
additional condition that the automorphism $\alpha$ map to the identity
automorphism of the image of $x$ in $\mathcal Y_T$; the projection
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}\to\mathcal X$ is again a 1-morphism. Both
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}$ and $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ are stacks
in groupoids whenever $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are
([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]), since automorphism data
satisfies effective descent in groupoids.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the finite-type assertion. Let $k$ be a field, let $n\ge1$, and put $d=\det(x_{ij})\in k[x_{ij}:1\le i,j\le n]$. Then $\operatorname{GL}_n=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_{ij},d^{-1}]$ is a group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) whose structure comorphisms are
$$\Delta(x_{ij})=\sum_{l=1}^{n}x_{il}\otimes x_{lj},\qquad\varepsilon(x_{ij})=\delta_{ij},\qquad S(x_{ij})=\text{the }(i,j)\text{-entry of }d^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(X),$$
and for every commutative unital $k$-algebra $R$ the group $\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ is the group of invertible $n\times n$ matrices over $R$. If $V$ is a $k$-vector space with basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$, then the functor $R\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_R(V\otimes_kR)$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{GL}_n$. In particular $\operatorname{GL}_1=\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ is the multiplicative group scheme, with $\Delta(t)=t\otimes t$, $\varepsilon(t)=1$ and $S(t)=t^{-1}$. For $V=0$ put $\operatorname{GL}_0=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the trivial group structure and $\operatorname{GL}_0(R)=\operatorname{Aut}_R(0)=\{1\}$; its coordinate ring is $k$ and its matrix has no entries. The coordinate constructions and point identifications are choice-free; AC is used for affine quasi-compactness in the finite-type assertion.
Assume AC. Every separated finite-type group scheme over a characteristic-zero field is smooth. No affineness, reducedness, or connectedness assumption is required.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a faithfully flat ring map $A\to B$, base change identifies $A$-modules with $B$-modules equipped with a descent isomorphism between their two pullbacks to $B\otimes_AB$, satisfying the cocycle identity over the triple tensor product. The same is true for commutative unital algebras, when transport is an algebra isomorphism. Writing transport as $\theta:N\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_AN$, the descended module or algebra is
$$D=\{n\in N:\theta(n\otimes1)=1\otimes n\},$$
and $B\otimes_AD\to N$, $b\otimes d\mapsto bd$, is an isomorphism respecting the datum.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $T\to[X/G]$ correspond to a left torsor $P\to T$ and an equivariant map $\phi:P\to X$. An object of $X\times_{[X/G]}T$ is a point $x\in X$ and an equivariant isomorphism from the trivial left torsor to $P$, compatible with $\phi$. Such an isomorphism is determined by the image $p\in P$ of the identity, and sends $g$ to $g p$; the compatibility condition forces $x=\phi(p)$. Thus $X\times_{[X/G]}T\cong P$. Since $P\to T$ is a torsor, it is a smooth surjective scheme morphism by [F3] and the local triviality in [F1]. Hence $X\to[X/G]$ is a representable smooth surjective atlas.

For two objects $(P,\phi)$ and $(P',\phi')$ over a scheme $T$, their isomorphism functor is the subfunctor of $\operatorname{Isom}_G(P,P')$ on which $\phi'\circ f=\phi$. After a common fppf cover trivializing both torsors, and after restricting to affine opens of the cover, $\operatorname{Isom}_G(P,P')\cong G\times T$. With the chosen trivializing sections $p,p'$, the condition is the inverse image of the diagonal $X\hookrightarrow X\times X$ under the two evaluation maps $f\mapsto(\phi'(f(p)),\phi(p))$. The diagonal of affine $X$ is closed, so this is a closed subscheme of $G\times T$, affine over $T$. The isomorphism functor therefore has affine local representatives with their canonical descent data; [F4] makes this affine descent datum effective. Thus the isomorphism functor is represented by an affine scheme over $T$, which proves the diagonal is affine, hence representable.

The torsor-with-map construction is a category fibred in groupoids by pullback. To verify the stack condition, take an fppf cover of $T$ and torsors with equivariant maps and compatible isomorphisms on its overlaps. The torsors are affine over their bases by [F4]. On affine opens of $T$, refine the cover by faithfully flat affine covers and apply the effective algebra descent of [F4]; its full faithfulness glues these descended affine schemes on overlaps. The action, torsor isomorphism $G\times P\simeq P\times_TP$, and maps to $X$ descend as scheme morphisms by [F1]. Their equivariance and compatibility identities can be checked after the cover, and the resulting $P\to T$ is fppf-locally the given torsor, hence is a torsor. Compatible isomorphisms descend uniquely in the same way, with inverses descending too. Thus morphisms form sheaves and every object descent datum is effective, exactly the stack condition of [F1].

By steps 1.1–1.3, the quotient stack has a smooth surjective representable atlas and representable diagonal. Step 1.3 establishes the stack condition, so the criterion in [F2] applies and $[X/G]$ is an algebraic stack. The inherited AC appears only in [A1] through those defining suppliers.

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver, in the convention of
[[def-path-ring-of-a-finite-quiver-over-the-integers]], and work over
$\mathbb C$. A **dimension vector** is a function
$\mathbf d:Q_0\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Put
$
V_i^{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C^{d_i},\qquad
\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)=
\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}
(V_i^{\mathbf d},V_j^{\mathbf d}),\qquad
G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}(V_i^{\mathbf d}).
$
The group acts by change of basis:
$(g\cdot X)_h=g_jX_hg_i^{-1}$. The **representation stack**
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)/G_{\mathbf d}]$
is the quotient stack: over a scheme $T$, its objects are left
$G_{\mathbf d}$-torsors $P\to T$ with equivariant maps
$P\to\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$;
arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with these maps. The
finite-dimensional atlas and the algebraic-stack conditions are verified in
[[lem-general-linear-quotient-stacks-are-algebraic]].

For two dimension vectors $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, write
$\mathbf d=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and choose
$V_i^{\mathbf d}=V_i^{\mathbf a}\oplus V_i^{\mathbf b}$. Let
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ be the vector space of
representations preserving $V^{\mathbf a}$. For an arrow $h:i\to j$, its
matrix has the form
$
X_h=
\begin{pmatrix}
X_h^{\mathbf a}&C_h\\
0&X_h^{\mathbf b}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad C_h\in\operatorname{Hom}(V_i^{\mathbf b},V_j^{\mathbf a}).
$
Let $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\subseteq G_{\mathbf d}$ be the subgroup preserving
the chosen graded subspaces. Define the **exact-sequence stack**
$
\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}].
$
Its maps are
$
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
\xrightarrow{\ p\ }\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}.
$
The map $q$ sends an exact sequence to its subrepresentation and quotient;
$p$ forgets the subrepresentation. Thus the order convention is
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf d}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$.
The block form shows that the off-diagonal extension parameters are the
coordinates $C_h$; it does not assert that extension classes are a vector
space after quotienting by automorphisms.

~~~tikzcd
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
& \mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
  \arrow[l,"q"'] \arrow[r,"p"]
& \mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}
~~~

The diagram records only the two maps just defined; it supplies no equality of
maps or algebraic operation by itself.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type
$\mathbb C$-scheme with an algebraic action of
$G=\prod_{r=1}^m\operatorname{GL}_{n_r,\mathbb C}$, allowing $n_r=0$.
Then the quotient stack $[X/G]$, defined by $G$-torsors with equivariant
maps to $X$, is an algebraic stack. The morphism $X\to[X/G]$ from the
trivial torsor is a smooth surjective representable atlas, and the diagonal
of $[X/G]$ is representable by affine schemes.

Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $k$. For $0\le r\le n$, $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ denotes the parameter set of $r$-dimensional linear subspaces of $V$. Thus $\operatorname{Gr}(0,V)=\{0\}$ and $\operatorname{Gr}(n,V)=\{V\}$. For $r<0$ or $r>n$ we set $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)=\varnothing$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every closed immersion of schemes is finite, hence
proper; the empty closed immersion is included, no Noetherian, reducedness or
nonemptiness hypothesis is used, and the Axiom of Choice enters through the
affine quotient structure of closed immersions and the properness of finite
morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S$ be a scheme and let $n\ge0$. Then the
structure morphism
$$\pi:\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
is proper. No Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed on $S$, and the empty base is included.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For every proper morphism $f:X\to S$ and
every morphism $S'\to S$, the base-changed morphism
$$f_{S'}:X\times_S S'\longrightarrow S'$$
is proper.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For proper morphisms of schemes
$X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$, the composition
$g\circ f:X\to S$ is proper.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the finite-type assertion. Let $k$ be a field, let $n\ge1$, and put $d=\det(x_{ij})\in k[x_{ij}:1\le i,j\le n]$. $$\Delta(x_{ij})=\sum_{l=1}^{n}x_{il}\otimes x_{lj},\qquad\varepsilon(x_{ij})=\delta_{ij},\qquad S(x_{ij})=\text{the }(i,j)\text{-entry of }d^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(X),$$
and for every commutative unital $k$-algebra $R$ the group $\operatorname{GL}_n(R)$ is the group of invertible $n\times n$ matrices over $R$. If $V$ is a $k$-vector space with basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$, then the functor $R\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_R(V\otimes_kR)$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{GL}_n$. In particular $\operatorname{GL}_1=\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ is the multiplicative group scheme, with $\Delta(t)=t\otimes t$, $\varepsilon(t)=1$ and $S(t)=t^{-1}$. The coordinate constructions and point identifications are choice-free; AC is used for affine quasi-compactness in the finite-type assertion.
Assume AC. Every separated finite-type group scheme over a characteristic-zero field is smooth. No affineness, reducedness, or connectedness assumption is required.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the relative Proj construction
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]).
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $E$ be a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_S$-module of locally constant rank $r\ge0$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Write
$$\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(E)$$
for the symmetric algebra of $E$
([[def-symmetric-algebra-qc-module]]): a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_S$-algebra ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]) with $\operatorname{Sym}^0(E)=\mathcal O_S$,
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$, generated as an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra by its
degree-one part $E$, and compatible with base change $S'\to S$
([[lem-symmetric-algebra-qc-and-base-change]]).

**Definition.** The **projective bundle** of $E$ over $S$ is the relative Proj
$$\pi:\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)\longrightarrow S,$$
with the relative twists $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(n)$, $n\in\mathbb Z$
([[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]). Since
$\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ is generated in degree one, the degree-one part
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$ generates the whole algebra, and there is a
canonical surjection
$$\pi^*E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1),$$
the **tautological quotient** of the pullback of $E$; it is locally given by
the coordinate sections of a projective space, over an open set on which
$E\cong\mathcal O_S^{\,r}$.

**Quotient convention.** This is the quotient (Grothendieck) convention: over
an $S$-scheme $g:T\to S$, an $S$-morphism $T\to\mathbb P_S(E)$ is the same as
an isomorphism class of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ invertible on $T$,
and the universal such quotient is the tautological quotient above; the
representing property is proved as [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]].
The associated affine construction is
$\mathbb V(E)=\operatorname{Spec}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)$; the rank-zero
case below displays its difference from $\mathbb P_S(E)$ over nonempty $S$.

**Rank zero.** If $E=0$ then $\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\mathcal O_S$ is
concentrated in degree $0$, its irrelevant ideal is $0$, and
$$\mathbb P_S(0)=\varnothing:$$
the total space is empty. This is consistent with the quotient convention,
because a surjection $0\to L$ onto an invertible sheaf exists only over the
empty scheme; the affine bundle $\mathbb V(0)=S$ is nonempty whenever $S$ is.

Let $F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets on
$(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]],
[[def-natural-transformation]]). It is **representable by algebraic spaces**
when for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to G$ the fibre product
$F\times_GT$ is an algebraic space over $S$
([[def-algebraic-space-as-fppf-sheaf]],
[[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). This generalizes
representability by schemes
([[def-representable-morphism-of-presheaves]]), under the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) of [[lem-scheme-functor-is-algebraic-space]]:
every morphism representable
by schemes is representable by algebraic spaces, because a scheme is an
algebraic space, and the fibre products agree. A property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces that is stable under base change
([[def-morphism-and-fibre-products-of-algebraic-spaces]]) is attributed
fibrewise to such a morphism: it **has property $\mathcal P$** when every base
change $F\times_GT\to T$ is a morphism of algebraic spaces with
$\mathcal P$. In this way one speaks of representable etale, smooth, flat,
surjective, open-immersion and closed-immersion morphisms of presheaves.

A **1-morphism of stacks in groupoids**
$f\colon\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$
([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) is **representable by algebraic
spaces** when for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every 1-morphism
$T\to\mathcal Y$ — equivalently, by the 2-Yoneda lemma, for every object
$x\in\mathcal Y_T$ — the 2-fibre product
$\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y,T}$ is equivalent to the stack in setoids
$\mathcal S_Z$ of an algebraic space $Z$ over $T$. Smooth, etale, surjective
and other fibrewise properties are then defined by base change to schemes, so
the definition specializes to the presheaf case when $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$
are stacks in setoids of presheaves of sets.

A morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ is **proper** if and only if it is separated,
of finite type, and universally closed. Here separatedness has the meaning of
[[def-separated-morphism-schemes]], finite type has the meaning of
[[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]], and universally closed
has the meaning of [[def-universally-closed-morphism]]. The definition applies
to arbitrary schemes: it assumes neither Noetherian hypotheses nor finite
presentation.

Let $p\colon\mathcal S\to(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ be a category fibred in
groupoids ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]) over the fppf site
([[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]). For a morphism $T'\to T$ of $S$-schemes
and an object $x$ of $\mathcal S$ over $T$ we write $x|_{T'}$ for the value of
a chosen pullback along $T'\to T$; different choices are canonically
isomorphic and the definitions below do not depend on them.

([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]). **Descent data** for a

$T_{ijk}$ (after pulling back along the three projections and using the
canonical identifications). With the evident notion of morphism — a family of
morphisms $x_i\to y_i$ compatible with the $\varphi_{ij}$ — these data form a
category $\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\},(x_i))$, and there is a base-change functor
$\mathcal S_T\to\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\})$ sending $x$ to
$(x|_{T_i},\text{canonical isomorphisms})$.

The fibred category $\mathcal S$ is a **prestack** when for all objects $x,y$
of $\mathcal S_T$ the presheaf
$$(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{fppf}\to\mathrm{Set},\qquad U\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal S_U}(x|_U,y|_U)$$
is an fppf sheaf ([[def-fppf-sheaf-and-sheafification]]); equivalently, for
every fppf covering the diagram of morphism sets is an equalizer.

The fibred category $\mathcal S$ is a **stack in groupoids** when it is a
prestack and every descent datum of objects is **effective**: for every fppf
covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ the base-change functor
$\mathcal S_T\to\mathrm{DD}(\{T_i\to T\})$ is an equivalence of categories.
Effectivity is thus the precise sense in which objects are glued from
descent data.

A presheaf of sets $F$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ determines a category
fibred in groupoids $\mathcal S_F$ whose fibre category over $T$ is the
**discrete groupoid** on the set $F(T)$ (the groupoid with only identity
morphisms). Descent data for $\mathcal S_F$ over a covering
$\{T_i\to T\}$ amount to a family of elements of the $F(T_i)$ whose
pullbacks agree on all $T_{ij}$, and effectivity amounts to gluing them to an
element of $F(T)$; consequently $\mathcal S_F$ is a stack in groupoids (a
**stack in setoids**) exactly when $F$ is an fppf sheaf. In particular, assuming the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in
[[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]], every
$S$-scheme $X$, whose represented presheaf is then an fppf sheaf, determines the
stack in groupoids $\mathcal S_X$ whose fibre category over $T$ is the
discrete groupoid on $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,X)$; this is the Yoneda
embedding of schemes into stacks.

An **algebraic stack** (or **Artin stack**) over $S$ is a stack in groupoids
$\mathcal X$ over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$
([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]],
[[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]) such that

1. the diagonal 1-morphism
   $\Delta\colon\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is representable by
   algebraic spaces ([[def-morphism-representable-by-algebraic-spaces]]), and
2. there exist an $S$-scheme $U$ and a 1-morphism
   $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ from the stack in setoids of $U$ which is
   representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth
   ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]).

Such a pair $(U,\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X)$ is called a **presentation** of
$\mathcal X$. The algebraic stack is **Deligne-Mumford** when a presentation
with $\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal X$ etale
([[def-etale-morphism-schemes]]) can be chosen. Under the inherited Axiom of
Choice for represented-sheaf descent ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]), a scheme, viewed as a stack
in setoids, is an algebraic stack with its
identity as presentation. An algebraic space is an algebraic stack using
any of its etale scheme covers as presentation; the identity is not a
scheme presentation when the algebraic space is not a scheme.

The **inertia stack** $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}$ is the category fibred in
groupoids whose fibre category over $T$ has as objects the pairs
$(x,\alpha)$ with $x$ an object of $\mathcal X_T$ and
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X_T}(x)$. For $f:T'\to T$, a morphism from $(y,\beta)$ over $T'$ to $(x,\alpha)$ over $T$ is an arrow $\gamma:y\to x$ of $\mathcal X$ over $f$ satisfying $\gamma\beta=\alpha\gamma$. Equivalently it is a vertical isomorphism $y\to f^*x$ intertwining $\beta$ with $f^*\alpha$. Composition is composition of these arrows; cartesian uniqueness supplies the pullback identifications. The **projection**
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$, $(x,\alpha)\mapsto x$, is a
1-morphism over $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$.

For a 1-morphism $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of stacks in groupoids, the
**relative inertia** $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ imposes the
additional condition that the automorphism $\alpha$ map to the identity
automorphism of the image of $x$ in $\mathcal Y_T$; the projection
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}\to\mathcal X$ is again a 1-morphism. Both
$\mathcal I_{\mathcal X}$ and $\mathcal I_{\mathcal X/\mathcal Y}$ are stacks
in groupoids whenever $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ are
([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]), since automorphism data
satisfies effective descent in groupoids.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a faithfully flat ring map $A\to B$, base change identifies $A$-modules with $B$-modules equipped with a descent isomorphism between their two pullbacks to $B\otimes_AB$, satisfying the cocycle identity over the triple tensor product. The same is true for commutative unital algebras, when transport is an algebra isomorphism. Writing transport as $\theta:N\otimes_AB\to B\otimes_AN$, the descended module or algebra is
$$D=\{n\in N:\theta(n\otimes1)=1\otimes n\},$$
and $B\otimes_AD\to N$, $b\otimes d\mapsto bd$, is an isomorphism respecting the datum.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to X$ be morphisms of
schemes and let $h:S'\to S$ be an arbitrary morphism, with base change
$f_{S'}:X\times_SS'\to S'$ as in [[def-base-change-morphism-schemes]].

1. If $f$ is smooth ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), then $f_{S'}$ is
   smooth.
2. If $f$ and $g$ are smooth, then the composite $f\circ g:Y\to S$ is smooth.
3. If $f$ is smooth at $x=g(y)$ and $g$ is smooth at $y$, then the relative
   dimensions ([[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]) add:
   $$\operatorname{reldim}_{f\circ g}(y)=\operatorname{reldim}_f(g(y))+\operatorname{reldim}_g(y).$$

The third clause is the chartwise additivity of relative dimensions; no
hypothesis is placed on $h$, and $X$, $S$, $S'$, $Y$ may be empty.

Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, let $x\in X$ and put $s=f(x)$.
The morphism $f$ is **smooth at $x$** when the following three conditions hold
at $x$:

1. $f$ is locally of finite presentation at $x$
   ([[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]);
2. $f$ is flat at $x$ ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]);
3. the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ ([[def-geometric-fibre]]) is
   geometrically regular at $x$, that is, for every field extension
   $K/\kappa(s)$ the local ring of $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}
   \operatorname{Spec}K$ at every point over $x$ is regular
   ([[def-ag-geometrically-regular-algebra-and-fibre]]).

The morphism $f$ is **smooth** if it is smooth at every point of $X$. A
morphism with empty source is smooth vacuously, and no condition is imposed
by an empty fibre: the pointwise clause of the definition is quantified over
primes of the fibre, of which there are none.

Smoothness is a condition on the germ of $f$ at $x$, so it is preserved by
restricting the source to an open neighbourhood of $x$ and by shrinking the
target to an open neighbourhood of $s$; affine-locally it becomes a condition
on a finitely presented ring map at a prime, and the equivalence with the
formal lifting and Jacobian formulations is proved on this page, not assumed
here. Relative dimension is defined separately, and in relative dimension
zero smoothness is equivalent to étaleness later on this page.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $\mathbf G_a=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ be the additive group scheme over $R$, with comultiplication $\Delta(t)=t\otimes1+1\otimes t$, counit $\varepsilon(t)=0$ and antipode $S(t)=-t$, so that $\mathbf G_a(T)=\mathcal O_T(T)$ as an additive group for every $S$-scheme $T$.

A **$\mathbf G_a$-torsor over $S$** is an $S$-scheme $\pi:X\to S$ that is faithfully flat and finitely presented, together with an action $\alpha:\mathbf G_a\times_SX\to X$ of $\mathbf G_a$ on $X$ over $S$ such that the shear morphism
$$\sigma:\mathbf G_a\times_SX\to X\times_SX,\qquad \sigma(g,x)=(g\cdot x,x)$$
is an isomorphism. Then $X$ is **trivial**: there is an isomorphism $X\cong\mathbf G_a\times_S S=\mathbf A^1_R$ of $S$-schemes, and in particular $\pi$ admits a section $S\to X$.

The Axiom of Choice enters through the fppf descent of scheme morphisms used below.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
The Plucker image of $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ is a closed projective algebraic set in $\mathbf P(\Lambda^rV)$, cut out by the quadratic Plucker relations.

For every $r$-subset $I$ of a basis of an $n$-dimensional $V$, the locus $p_I\ne0$ in $\operatorname{Gr}(r,V)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A_k^{r(n-r)}$; these loci cover the Grassmannian and have regular transition maps.

derivations.claim: Put $Y=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$. The block description makes $Y$ an affine finite-type scheme. The block parabolic is $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}=U\rtimes L$ with underlying scheme $\mathbb A^u\times L$, where $L=G_{\mathbf a}\times G_{\mathbf b}$; hence $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$ is affine and finite type, and it is smooth because $U$ is a vector group and each general linear factor of $L$ is smooth by [F5]. The quotient definition in [F1] makes $Y\to[Y/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}]$ representable: after base change by a scheme $T\to[Y/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}]$ corresponding to a $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$-torsor $R\to T$, the pullback is $R$. Fppf-local triviality and [F8] make this torsor an affine scheme over $T$. To see that $R\to T$ is smooth, extend its structure group to $G_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$; the resulting $G$-torsor is a tuple of frame bundles of vector bundles $E_i$, while the reduction to $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$ specifies subbundles $F_i\subset E_i$ of ranks $a_i$ with locally free quotients. Zariski-locally these sequences split and the bundles admit adapted frames, so $R\to T$ is locally $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\times T\to T$, which is smooth by [F9] and [F10]; it is surjective as a torsor. For two underlying $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$-torsors $R,R'$ over $T$, their equivariant isomorphism functor is fppf-locally represented by $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\times T$, and these affine local representatives descend by [F8]. Fppf-locally trivialize both torsors, with their equivariant maps given by $y,y':T'\to Y$. The compatible isomorphisms are cut out in $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\times T'$ by $g\cdot y=y'$, the inverse image of $\Delta_Y$ under $(g,t)\mapsto(g\cdot y(t),y'(t))$. This is closed because $Y$ is separated, and the closed subscheme descends effectively by [F8]. Thus the diagonal is affine representable. Effective descent of torsors with maps is obtained by descending their affine schemes, actions and compatible maps by the affine-descent argument in the proof of [F2]; that argument uses only affineness of the group and target, so also applies to this parabolic and to its vector subgroup $U$. By [F8], $[Y/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}]$ is an algebraic stack. Now, for each arrow $h:i\to j$, the free off-diagonal block is $\operatorname{Hom}(V_i^{\mathbf b},V_j^{\mathbf a})$; hence $Y\to \operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a)\times\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf b)$ is a vector bundle of rank $e=\sum_{h:i\to j}b_i a_j$. The kernel $U$ of $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to L$ consists of upper-right vertex blocks and has dimension $u=\sum_i a_i b_i$.

First construct the relative Grassmannian used here. For a rank-$n$ bundle $E$ on any scheme $T$ and $0\le a\le n$, impose the homogeneous Plucker relations of [F3] in $\mathbb P_T((\bigwedge^a E)^\vee)$. On a frame chart with $p_I\ne0$, normalize $p_I=1$. The one-replacement coordinates give the entries of a matrix with identity pivot rows; the Plucker relation expressing a coordinate with $s$ nonpivot indices in terms of coordinates with fewer such indices proves inductively that every coordinate is its corresponding maximal minor. This is the calculation in [F3], using polynomial identities and only inversion of $p_I$, hence valid over every $\mathbb C$-algebra, including nonreduced ones. Conversely those minors satisfy all relations by alternating multilinearity. Thus each chart has polynomial coordinate ring in $a(n-a)$ entries and represents graph subbundles whose projection onto the pivot summand is invertible. Any locally direct-summand rank-$a$ subbundle is covered by such charts, since its maximal minors generate the unit ideal. The minor-ratio transitions identify the same subbundle, so the charts represent the subbundle functor, glue under change of frame, and give a closed relative Plucker embedding. Ranks $0,n$ give $T$. Now let an arbitrary scheme $T$ map to $\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$. By the quotient-stack definition this is a family of vector bundles $E_i$ of ranks $a_i+b_i$, with arrow maps. The base change of $p$ parametrizes subbundles $F_i\subset E_i$ of ranks $a_i$ preserved by every arrow. It is the closed subscheme of the relative Grassmannian $\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}_T(a_i,E_i)$ cut out by the vanishing of the bundle maps $F_i\to E_j\to E_j/F_j$ for each arrow $h:i\to j$. The relative Plucker map sends $F_i$ to the line subbundle $\det(F_i)\subseteq\bigwedge^{a_i}E_i$. Under the quotient convention of [[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], this is represented by the quotient line of $(\bigwedge^{a_i}E_i)^\vee$ obtained by dualizing the inclusion. Thus each relative Grassmannian is a closed subscheme of $\mathbb P_T((\bigwedge^{a_i}E_i)^\vee)$; on local frames this is the closed embedding just constructed from [F3], and the equations glue under changes of frame. Each such projective bundle is proper: after any base change $T'\to T$, trivialize $E_i$ over an open cover of $T'$; on each open the projection is a projective-space projection, hence proper by [F4]. The image of a closed set is closed on each member of the cover and therefore closed globally; separatedness and finite type are also local on the base. Thus every base change is proper by [F7]. The product of these proper maps is proper by base change and composition [F4]. The arrow conditions are closed because they are zero loci of regular bundle maps, so the incidence scheme is proper over $T$ as a closed subscheme of that product [F4]. In the standard frame atlas this scheme is exactly $ I_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}= \{(X,(F_i)):\dim F_i=a_i,\ X_h(F_i)\subseteq F_j \text{ for every }h:i\to j\}. $, and its defining equations are the same zero-locus equations just described; in an ordinary Grassmannian chart they are the vanishing of the complementary matrix block. Hence every scheme base change of $p$ is a proper scheme.

Pull back $q$ along the atlas $Z=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a)\times\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf b) \to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$. This fixes the endpoint representations. Every middle representation is a block matrix from step 1.1, and every isomorphism inducing the identity on the fixed endpoints is a unique upper-right vertex block. Hence the pullback stack is $[Y/U]\to Z$, where $Y\to Z$ is the rank-$e$ vector bundle of off-diagonal blocks and $U$ is the rank-$u$ vector group of changes of splitting. For any scheme $T\to[Y/U]$, its base change is a $U\cong\mathbb G_a^u$-torsor, represented by an affine scheme using [F8]. Cover $T$ by affine opens. On each affine base, choose an affine fppf cover of the torsor as in [F11]; the unique group element between the two pulled-back torsor points is a vector $\delta\in(B\otimes_A B)^u$ satisfying the additive Amitsur $1$-cocycle equation coordinatewise. Exactness in [F11] gives $b\in B^u$ with $\delta=b\otimes1-1\otimes b$, and translation by $b$ descends a section, trivializing the torsor there. Thus $Y\to[Y/U]$ is Zariski-locally $U\times T\to T$, which is smooth by [F9] and [F10], and it is surjective as a torsor. The same inverse-image-of-$\Delta_Y$ argument as in step 1.1, with $U$ in place of $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$, gives $[Y/U]$ an affine representable diagonal, so it is an algebraic stack. Its composite $Y\to Z$ is a vector bundle projection of relative dimension $e$. By the atlas convention just stated, $[Y/U]\to Z$ is smooth of relative stack dimension $e-u$. Smoothness and relative dimension are checked after the displayed smooth target atlas, so the same holds for $q$. Substitution of the definition of $\chi_Q$ gives $e-u=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, including arrows that are loops or occur with multiplicity.

The construction in step 1.2 identifies every scheme base change of $p$ with the incidence scheme, so [F7] proves that $p$ is representable by schemes, hence by algebraic spaces; the same step proves every such base-changed map is proper. If some $a_i=0$ or $a_i=a_i+b_i$, the corresponding Grassmannian is a point and the same closed-incidence argument applies. Step 2.1 proves the smoothness of $q$, so both claims of the Statement follow. AC is used only through [A1].

Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: First refine as in [F2] to respect the zero fibre. On each irreducible component of a smooth stratum where $f$ is nonconstant, [F5] gives a nonempty open of the affine line over which its differential is onto. Its proper closed complement is finite by [F1]. There are finitely many stratum components, and constant strata have one value each, so excluding the finitely many nonzero exceptional values leaves no interior stratum critical point over a sufficiently small punctured disc.

For a nonconstant stratum $S$ of dimension $s$, close in $\mathbb C^M\times(\mathbb C^M)^*$ the locus $C_S^\circ=\{(x,\xi):x\in S,\ f(x)\ne0,\ df|_{T_xS}\ne0,\ \xi|_{T_xS}\in\mathbb C\,df_x\}$. Its covector fibre has dimension $M-s+1$, so every component of its closure $C_S$ has dimension $M+1$. The function $f$ is nonconstant on each base component, and its zero fibre is a proper closed subset there. Hence $\Lambda_S=C_S\cap\{f(x)=0\}$ has dimension at most $M$. The closure includes base points in lower strata; no unproved relative Thom condition is being assumed.

Identify covectors with their coefficient vectors and consider $F:\Lambda_S\times\overline{\Lambda_S}\to\mathbb C^M\times\mathbb C^M$, $F(x,\xi,y,\eta)=(x-\eta,y-\xi)$. Its source has dimension at most $2M$: applying the generic-fibre formula to the projection of each product component gives the sum of the two component dimensions. For each dominant irreducible component [F1] gives zero-dimensional, hence finite, fibres on a nonempty target Zariski open; exclude the closed image closure of each nondominant component. A common nonempty open $O$ therefore has finite fibres. The real diagonal $a\mapsto(a,\bar a)$ meets $O$ densely in every real open set: a nonzero polynomial vanishing on its proper algebraic complement remains nonzero after the invertible substitution $(a,b)=(u+iv,u-iv)$, and cannot vanish on a real open box, by induction on the number of variables using the finite-root property of each nonzero one-variable polynomial. Intersect these finitely many good parameter sets for all the strata.

On a complex tangent space $T_xS$ where $df$ is onto, put $\ell=d|x-a|^2|_{T_xS}$. At a transverse sphere point $\ell\ne0$. The restriction of $df$ to $\ker\ell$ then fails to be onto exactly when $\ell$ is a real linear combination of $\operatorname{Re}df$ and $\operatorname{Im}df$. Indeed a real covector on the target annihilating the image of $\ker\ell$ pulls back to a multiple of $\ell$, and the converse is immediate. A nontransverse sphere point is separately a bad boundary point: there $\ell=0$, so it also satisfies the covector inclusion below. Identifying real covectors with real parts of complex covectors, the obstruction is $\bar x-\bar a\in N^*_{S,x}+\mathbb C\,df_x$.

The good relative-conormal centre set of step 3.1 is Euclidean open and dense. Apply [F7] within its intersection with an arbitrarily small real open neighborhood of $p$, obtaining such a centre $a$ for which the ordinary distance has only finitely many critical points on all strata. In addition to $E_a$, avoid their finitely many critical distances when choosing the radius. Thus the sphere is transverse to all strata, including those inside $f=0$. The set $E_a=\{x\in X\cap f^{-1}(0):(x,\bar x-\bar a)\in\Lambda_S\text{ for some }S\}$ is finite: every such $x$ gives $(x,\bar x-\bar a,\bar x,x-a)$ in the finite fibre of $F$ over $(a,\bar a)$. Choose $\epsilon>|a-p|$ avoiding the finitely many distances $|x-a|$ for $x\in E_a$. This choice is cofinal. Inside a prescribed $B_R(p)$ choose $|a-p|<R/4$ and $\epsilon\in(R/3,R/2)$ avoiding those distances; then $p$ lies in the ball and its closed ball lies in $B_R(p)$.

If no sufficiently small punctured tube avoided that obstruction on the sphere, there would be $x_j\in S\cap\partial B_\epsilon(a)$ with $f(x_j)\ne0$, $f(x_j)\to0$ and the obstruction of step 3.2. Compactness of $X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)$ and finiteness of the strata give a subsequence in one $S$ converging to $x_0\in X\cap\partial B_\epsilon(a)\cap f^{-1}(0)$. Step 3.2 gives $(x_j,\bar x_j-\bar a)\in C_S$, so its limit belongs to $\Lambda_S$. Thus $x_0\in E_a$ and $|x_0-a|=\epsilon$, contradicting step 4.1. There is consequently $\delta>0$ with no sphere obstruction for $0<|f|<\sqrt2\delta$, and shrink it also as in step 1.1.

Over the punctured rectangle, the sphere is transverse to every input stratum and $f$ is submersive on both its interior and boundary intersections by steps 1.1, 3.2 and 5.1. Transverse intersection with a smooth hypersurface preserves Whitney conditions: the limiting tangent planes intersect its tangent kernel in the expected dimension, and the first-order Taylor formula puts limiting fibre secants in that kernel. Thus the interior/sphere intersections are a finite Whitney stratification. The closed-ball tube is proper over this base since inverse images of compact base subsets are closed in the compact $X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)$. The actual hypotheses of [F3] therefore hold, and its transports preserve the boundary stratum and hence the interior.

On a contractible half-rectangle, fixed ordered coordinate paths and [F3]'s compact-path transports give local products and inverses. The coefficient reconstruction of [F4] transports $A$ on these products; finite interval subdivisions glue the comparisons, and reversing transport gives inverse cochain maps. These local coefficient comparisons preserve the marked boundary and therefore restrict to the open-ball interior; the global finite fibre models are constructed in the final step below. Step 4.1 supplies a cofinal family; intersecting with arbitrarily small function rectangles retains cofinality at $p$. Smooth affine charts reduce the last assertion to this construction. This proves the transport assertion.

Replace the rectangle by a small circular function disc and consider $W=X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)\cap\{|f|\le\delta\}$. No triangulation of the real cut $\operatorname{Re}f=0$ or of an arbitrary map has been claimed. Together with step 7.1 this proves the stated conclusions, with AC exactly through [A1].

Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, $X$ a smooth $K$-scheme of finite type and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a coherent ideal sheaf that is not identically zero on any irreducible component of $X$ ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]).
Then there is a canonical principalization of $\mathcal I$: a sequence
$$X=X_0\leftarrow X_1\leftarrow\dots\leftarrow X_r=\widetilde X$$
of blowups of regular centers $C_{i-1}\subseteq X_{i-1}$ ([[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]]) such that
(a) the exceptional divisor $E_i$ of the composite $\sigma_i\colon X_i\to X$ has only simple normal crossings and $C_{i-1}$ has SNC with $E_{i-1}$ ([[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]]);
(b) the total transform $\sigma_r^*\mathcal I$ is the ideal of an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings support $\widetilde E$ which is a natural combination of the irreducible components of $E_r$.
The morphism $(\widetilde X,\sigma_r^*\mathcal I)\to(X,\mathcal I)$ commutes with smooth morphisms and with embeddings of ambient smooth schemes, and is equivariant under every group action on $X$ preserving $\mathcal I$ (not necessarily preserving $K$).

Let $X$ be a regular locally Noetherian scheme of pure dimension $n$ ([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]).
A reduced effective Cartier divisor $D\subseteq X$ ([[def-effective-cartier-divisor]], [[def-cartier-divisor]]) is a strict normal crossings divisor (an SNC divisor) if for every point $p\in X$, writing $d_p=\dim\mathcal O_{X,p}$, there is a regular system of parameters $u_1,\dots,u_{d_p}$ of $\mathcal O_{X,p}$ and a subset $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d_p\}$ such that the ideal of $D$ in $\mathcal O_{X,p}$ is generated by $\prod_{j\in J}u_j$; equivalently, every irreducible component of $D$ is regular and the local equations of the components through $p$ extend to a regular system of parameters.
A finite family $E=\{D_1,\dots,D_m\}$ of reduced effective Cartier divisors on $X$ is in simultaneous SNC position if for every subset $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$ the union of components of the divisors in $J$ is an SNC divisor; equivalently, at every point $p$ the union of all components of members of $E$ passing through $p$ is cut out by a subset of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{X,p}$.
For the marked-ideal algorithm on this page, the irreducible components within each individual member of $E$ must be pairwise disjoint, and no irreducible component is repeated in different members. Thus at a point each member contributes at most one distinct parameter equation. This is the additional boundary convention of Włodarczyk, Definition 2.1.1. Such a family $E$ always carries a fixed total order, and the members of $E$ play the role of the exceptional divisors of a multiple test blow-up.

Let $P=\{\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$, $Q=\{\operatorname{Re}g\le0\}$ and $Z=\{\operatorname{Re}(f+g)\le0\}$. On cofinal neighborhoods $U,V$ from [F3], put $A_+=U\setminus P$, $B_+=V\setminus Q$ and $L=(A_+\times V)\cup(U\times B_+)$. These are open complements, not asserted CW subcomplexes. Localization represents their support cochains by the relative complexes of $(U,A_+)$, $(V,B_+)$ and $(U\times V,L)$. The finite ordinary and Milnor-fibre models in [F3], including its compact-tube triangulation, give finite homology of $U,A_+$ and their relative pair, and similarly for $V,B_+$. No triangulation of the real cuts $P,Q$ is needed.

Here is the required local duality calculation. If closed $Z_+,Z_-$ cover a locally compact space, with $L=Z_+\cap Z_-$ and inclusions $j_\pm,m$, their localization triangles give $m^*j_{+*}j_+^!A\simeq(L\to Z_-)^!j_-^*A$. To verify it, apply $j_{+*}j_+^!$ to localization for $Z_-$: the open-complement term is unchanged by support in $Z_+$ because $X\setminus Z_-\subset Z_+$, and becomes zero after restriction to $L$. Closed proper base change identifies the remaining term as stated. Dualizing these adjunction maps exchanges the two support descriptions. This calculation uses the analytic exceptional adjunction of [F1]. On the present local sector pairs, [F3] and [F4] give finite cochain and relative-cochain complexes, so dualization and evaluation are the ordinary finite-vector-space operations; no biduality theorem for arbitrary nonconstructible analytic sheaves is being invoked.

To prove standard-coefficient constructibility, treat constant-function components directly and otherwise apply [F5] to $(f)$. Obtain $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ proper, smooth upstairs, isomorphic off $f=0$, with $f\pi$ having SNC zero support. The support-centre clause in [F5] and the ordinary Rees-algebra blowup charts imply the asserted isomorphism off $f=0$ at every step. Thus $\mathbb Q_X\to R\pi_*\mathbb Q_{\widetilde X}$ is an isomorphism there, and $\Psi$, which depends only on $j^*A$, gives $\Psi_f\mathbb Q_X\simeq R\pi_{0*}\Psi_{f\pi}\mathbb Q_{\widetilde X}$ by step 2.1. This uses principalization of the function ideal, not resolution of the ambient variety alone.

Here is the open-pair extension of the relative AW comparison. Write $N=C_*(A_+\times V)+C_*(U\times B_+)$ and $E=C_*(U\times V)/N$. By naturality [F7], AW, shuffle and their homotopies descend to a chain homotopy equivalence between $E$ and $C_*(U,A_+)\otimes C_*(V,B_+)$. The two indicated open sets cover $L$, so [F8] gives a small-chain retraction $R$ on $C_*(L)$ landing in $N$, with $1-R=dD+Dd$, and both $R,D$ preserve $N$. Thus $D$ contracts $J=C_*(L)/N$. Extend its contraction to a graded map $e:E\to J$ by zero on the remaining singular-simplex basis vectors. Then $T=1-de-ed$ commutes with the differential and kills $J$. It factors through a chain inverse to $q:E\to C_*(U\times V,L)$, since $qT=q$ and $T|_J=0$; its other composite is homotopic to the identity by $e$. This proves the relative chain comparison for these OPEN pairs. Subdivision depth is chosen separately for each simplex by [F8], never uniformly over all chains.

In SNC coordinates $f\pi=u(z)\prod_{i=1}^r z_i^{m_i}$ with $u\ne0$ and $m_i\ge1$. By [F6] choose a local $m_1$-st root $v$ of $u$; replacing $z_1$ by $v(z)z_1$ is an invertible coordinate change along the SNC stratum and makes the function the monomial. For small $t\ne0$ in a coordinate polydisc, put $s_i=-\log|z_i|$. The radial equation is the open convex simplex $s_i>L_i$, $\sum_i m_i s_i=-\log|t|$. The angular fibre of $\prod_i e^{im_i\theta_i}=t/|t|$ has $\gcd(m_i)$ components, each a torus $(S^1)^{r-1}$: the Euclidean algorithm extends the primitive integer row $(m_i/\gcd(m_i))$ to an invertible integer matrix, reducing its torus character to the $\gcd(m_i)$-power map in one coordinate. The tangential coordinate disc is contractible. These are finite cellular cochain models, constant in each tangential chart, and their coordinate-change transport gives locally constant finite-rank cohomology on the finitely many algebraic SNC strata. Thus $\Psi_{f\pi}\mathbb Q$ is bounded algebraically constructible.

Over $\mathbb Q$, the finite-dimensional relative homology in step 2.2 is free. The algebraic part of [F7]'s relative cohomological proof applies to the free relative singular complexes with the chain comparison now proved in step 3.2: choose cycle/boundary sections, split one factor up to chain homotopy onto its homology with zero differential, and use the finite-basis evaluation inverse $w\mapsto\sum_i w(-\otimes e_i)\otimes e_i^*$. There are finitely many terms in each degree and bounded finite homology; these maps identify the actual cochain cross product with a quasi-isomorphism. Constant shifts, external products and smooth pullbacks of these constant inputs preserve this comparison. The support-product morphism itself is natural for arbitrary coefficient morphisms: tensor supported sections on the two factors and then include their product support, and apply the same map on derived resolutions. This naturality does not assert an isomorphism on an arbitrary proper-image input. Passing through the cofinal stalk system gives $R\Gamma_PA\boxtimes R\Gamma_QB\simeq R\Gamma_{P\times Q}(A\boxtimes B)$ for the standard inputs used here. Compose it with inclusion of supports $P\times Q\subset Z$ and restrict to the product zero fibre to define TS. This proof neither applies the CW-pair theorem to an open complement nor invokes algebraic biduality on real half-spaces.

Proper constructible preservation [F2] applied to $\pi_0$ and step 3.1 proves bounded algebraic constructibility of $\Psi_f\mathbb Q_X$, and its natural cone in step 1.1 proves the same for $V_f\mathbb Q_X$. The local relative models of [F3] and [F4] give a uniform finite bound depending on $\dim X$ for its ordinary amplitude. Standard coefficients on smooth frame charts are pullbacks by the argument below, so their unshifted amplitude equals that downstairs, independently of the auxiliary frame dimension. Constant shifts, external products and ordinary Verdier duals stay within the proved constructible domain of [F2]; proper images do by [F2] and the comparison of step 2.1. This is constructible preservation, not an additional claim of Thom–Sebastiani invertibility on every such proper image.

To prove this TS map is an isomorphism, work on a product of cofinal neighborhoods [F3], and set $\Theta=(\operatorname{Re}f,\operatorname{Re}g)$, $C=\{u\le0,v\le0\}$, $D=\{u+v\le0\}$. Localization identifies the required support comparison with restriction of complement cochains from $\Theta^{-1}(C^c)$ to $\Theta^{-1}(D^c)$. On $u>0,v<0$ deform by $H_t(u,v)=(u,(1-t)v+t\max(v,-u/2))$; on $u<0,v>0$ use the exchanged formula, and on the northeast quadrant and its positive axes use the identity. The formulas agree continuously in $C^c$, never move a coordinate through zero, do not increase absolute coordinates, send $C^c$ into $D^c$ at $t=1$, and preserve $D^c$ throughout. Thus they supply a homotopy inverse to the complement inclusion. Leave imaginary coordinates fixed and lift these paths by [F3]'s product sector transports, preserving the marked sphere boundaries and coefficients. The finite relative cochain comparisons [F4] identify restriction with a quasi-isomorphism, not merely an equality of dimensions. Cofinality and stalk detection prove that the TS map of step 4.2 is an isomorphism.

For a smooth map $s:E\to X$, local product coordinates make $fs$ the pullback function and make the relative half-space pair a complex ball times the base pair. Its ordinary cochain complex is $\mathbb Q$, so [F4] gives the natural comparison $s^*V_fA\simeq V_{fs}s^*A$. It is the inverse-image map of the localization triangles and is therefore compatible with changes of product chart, composition and all support-product maps. For three functions both iterated TS maps are induced by the same inclusion $\prod_i\{\operatorname{Re}f_i\le0\}\subset\{\operatorname{Re}\sum_i f_i\le0\}$. Proper commutation of $V$ can also be seen directly: localization for $\{\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$, proper base change for its open complement and the identity on the middle object identify its support triangle after $Rp_*$ with the support triangle downstairs. Proper restriction to $f=0$ then gives $V_fRp_*\simeq Rp_*V_{fp}$. Applying it to the ordinary unit gives $V_f\mathbb Q_X\to Rp_*V_{fp}\mathbb Q_E$. For composable proper maps the unit of the composite is the composite of units, so these coefficient maps compose. Naturality of the external-support map of step 4.2 on that unit proves compatibility with TS and external products.

Apply the same construction to $e^{-i\theta}f$ and $e^{-i\theta}g$. Use circular function discs inside the rectangles of [F3]; these are independent of $\theta$. Transport from $\theta=0$ to $2\pi$ is the positive-loop monodromy of $f+g$, and on the external product it is the simultaneous transport $T_f\otimes T_g$. TS therefore intertwines these automorphisms, without semisimplicity. This also constructs the angular comparisons used in step 1.1.

Apply step 2.3 to $Z_\pm=\{\pm\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$. On $L=\{\operatorname{Re}f=0\}$ the restricted support complex is locally supported on $f=0$ near that fibre: at any other sufficiently nearby value $it\ne0$, the submersion product [F3] has zero half-space relative complex. On a closed inclusion whose intersection with a complex's support is open and closed relative to that support, ordinary and exceptional restriction agree; factor through the support and use its open restriction adjunction to verify the natural map. Thus restricting the dual calculation from $L$ to $f=0$ gives $D V_fA\simeq V_f^\pi DA$, the opposite-half-space normalization. The specified angular half-turn of step 7.1 identifies it with $V_fDA$. For the standard coefficient and its proved constructible closure [F2] applies; since $D\mathbb Q_X=\mathbb Q_X[2\dim X]$, this proves the claimed normalized duality formula. On the dual coefficient the monodromy is contragredient transport $D(T^{-1})$, making evaluation invariant; all preceding maps respect this transport by naturality.

The maps in steps 2.2–8.1 are the maps of the same support triangles, external adjunctions, orientations and specified angular transports. Their composition and proper/smooth pasting identities therefore hold simultaneously by [F1]; duality takes these identities to the corresponding identities for dual coefficients. Steps 3.1–5.1 put every standard coefficient and the stated closure in the actual constructible domain, and step 5.2 proves the load-bearing TS isomorphism. This proves all assertions, with AC exactly as in [A1].

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver, in the convention of
[[def-path-ring-of-a-finite-quiver-over-the-integers]], and work over
$\mathbb C$. A **dimension vector** is a function
$\mathbf d:Q_0\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Put
$
V_i^{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C^{d_i},\qquad
\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)=
\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}
(V_i^{\mathbf d},V_j^{\mathbf d}),\qquad
G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}(V_i^{\mathbf d}).
$
The group acts by change of basis:
$(g\cdot X)_h=g_jX_hg_i^{-1}$. The **representation stack**
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)/G_{\mathbf d}]$
is the quotient stack: over a scheme $T$, its objects are left
$G_{\mathbf d}$-torsors $P\to T$ with equivariant maps
$P\to\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$;
arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with these maps. The
finite-dimensional atlas and the algebraic-stack conditions are verified in
[[lem-general-linear-quotient-stacks-are-algebraic]].

For two dimension vectors $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, write
$\mathbf d=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and choose
$V_i^{\mathbf d}=V_i^{\mathbf a}\oplus V_i^{\mathbf b}$. Let
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ be the vector space of
representations preserving $V^{\mathbf a}$. For an arrow $h:i\to j$, its
matrix has the form
$
X_h=
\begin{pmatrix}
X_h^{\mathbf a}&C_h\\
0&X_h^{\mathbf b}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad C_h\in\operatorname{Hom}(V_i^{\mathbf b},V_j^{\mathbf a}).
$
Let $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\subseteq G_{\mathbf d}$ be the subgroup preserving
the chosen graded subspaces. Define the **exact-sequence stack**
$
\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}].
$
Its maps are
$
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
\xrightarrow{\ p\ }\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}.
$
The map $q$ sends an exact sequence to its subrepresentation and quotient;
$p$ forgets the subrepresentation. Thus the order convention is
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf d}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$.
The block form shows that the off-diagonal extension parameters are the
coordinates $C_h$; it does not assert that extension classes are a vector
space after quotienting by automorphisms.

~~~tikzcd
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
& \mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
  \arrow[l,"q"'] \arrow[r,"p"]
& \mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}
~~~

The diagram records only the two maps just defined; it supplies no equality of
maps or algebraic operation by itself.

Assume AC. Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$ be
dimension vectors. In the notation of
[[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]], the
map $q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$ is a smooth morphism of
algebraic stacks of relative complex dimension
$
r_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)
=\sum_{h:i\to j} b_i a_j-\sum_{i\in Q_0}a_i b_i
=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),
$
where
$
\chi_Q(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)
=\sum_i u_i v_i-\sum_{h:i\to j}u_i v_j.
$
The forgetful map $p:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$ is representable and proper. These claims
allow loops, multiple arrows, zero coordinates, and the empty quiver.

Assume AC as inherited from [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. For a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with an algebraic action of a finite product $G$ of general linear groups, put $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$. The **intrinsic quotient-stack Borel–Moore grading** of this presentation is
$$\mathbb H_i([X/G];\mathbb Q)=H_{i+2g}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;\mathbb Q).$$
The group on the right has exactly the variety dualizing normalization of the cited supplier, $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$. Equivalently, for a sufficiently acyclic free general linear frame space $U$ of dimension $t$, the group is the stable value $H_{i+2t}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;\mathbb Q)$ in each fixed degree. There is no one finite approximation asserted to compute all degrees.

For representation stacks use $X=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$ and $G=G_{\mathbf d}$ from [[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]]. For an extension or flag presentation $[Y/P]$ with total-dimension group $G$ and block parabolic $P$, use the induced variety $S=G\times_PY$ and set $\mathbb H_i([Y/P])=H_{i+2\dim G}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(S)$. The induction and frame comparisons for these presentations are proved in [[lem-quiver-parabolic-levi-borel-model-comparisons]]; this formula does not assert presentation independence for arbitrary Artin stacks.

If $X$ is smooth of dimension $x$, write $D=x-g$. Then $\mathbb H_i([X/G])=H_G^{2D-i}(X;\mathbb Q)$. The complex orientation, rational coefficients and the intrinsic shift are part of this convention. No Tate enrichment is included. Rank-zero general linear factors are omitted and the empty product is the trivial group.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has
characteristic zero, and that a finite product
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups
acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]).
For equivariant algebraic maps between such varieties, the coherent ordinary
six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category
$D^b_{G,c}$:

1. the functors $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!$ are defined on $D^b_{G,c}$, with
   $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, and the tensor and internal-Hom
   adjunction $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$;
2. composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection
   formula and the trace hold, and for a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$,
   $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ the exchange
   $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey
   Cartesian pasting; proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$;
3. the normalized dualizing object $\omega^G$ restricts to the ordinary
   $\omega_X$ of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]],
   and for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ one has
   $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$; this is not the unnormalized quotient-stack
   dualizing shift.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $U_N$ has the right action $u\cdot g=u\circ g$ and the quotient uses
$(u,x)\cdot g=(ug,g^{-1}x)$. For the action nerve use the equivalent left
action $g\cdot(u,x)=(ug^{-1},gx)$, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$ and $B_N$ are points and $X_N=X$, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

The finite local comparisons do not assert a global tensor splitting for an
arbitrary bundle with fibre $U_N$, such as the comparison projections
$X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $X_{N,M}\to X_M$.

locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of

$$U_N=\prod_{i=1}^{s}\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad r_N=2\min_{i}(N_i-n_i),$$
where $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is the open set of
injective, equivalently full-rank, complex $N\times n$ matrices. Then:

1. each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to
   the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)=\{A\in\mathbb C^{N\times n}:A^*A=I_n\}$
   of orthonormal frames
   ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]]);
2. each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold and is
   homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the map
   $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ forgetting the last column is a
   numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a
   Hurewicz and a Serre fibration;
3. $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.
