The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Write the ordered decomposition as $V_i=\bigoplus_{r=1}^s V_i^r$ and put $d_i^r=\dim V_i^r$. At each vertex, the partial flag variety is the closed incidence locus in $\prod_{r=1}^{s-1}\operatorname{Gr}(\sum_{j\le r}d_i^j,V_i)$: adjacent inclusions are the zero loci of the tautological subbundle maps to the next quotient bundle. It is projective by the relative Plucker construction of [F1]. On the open locus of flags transverse to an opposite coordinate block flag, successive elimination gives a unique block lower unitriangular adapted matrix; its entries are regular ratios of the invertible pivot minors. Its columns give an algebraic section of $G\to G/P$. Permuting the coordinate pivots gives finitely many such charts covering all flags. The incidence locus of pairs consisting of a representation and a preserved flag is closed in $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)\times G/P$, since each arrow's map from a flag subbundle to the corresponding quotient must vanish. The adapted-frame sections identify it locally with the product of the flag chart and the upper-block vector space $Y$, with transition action $P$; hence it is $S=G\times_PY$, a separated quasi-projective finite-type variety. The space $G/L$ is the open locus of tuples of subspaces of ranks $d_i^r$ whose direct sum is $V_i$, in the corresponding product of Grassmannians. Taking the normalized pivot frame in each summand gives algebraic local sections of $G\to G/L$. The incidence locus in $\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)\times G/L$ requiring preservation of each cumulative sum is closed there; these sections identify it with $T=G\times_LY$. Thus $T$ too is separated, quasi-projective and finite type. The quotient equivalences $[S/G]\simeq[Y/P]$ and $[T/G]\simeq[Y/L]$ extend and reduce principal bundles; the section charts show that these constructions are inverse, including their equivariant maps. Zero ranks and repeated flag stages impose no extra condition; omit their factors. Empty products are points.

We need a graded identification B_*([T/G]) = B_*([Y/L]) (2) with the same intrinsic convention of [F2] on both sides. On a G-frame model U, T x_G U = Y x_L U. To compare this with a usual L-frame model V, use R=(Y x U x V)/L. The projections to (Y x U)/L and (Y x V)/L are locally trivial fibrations with fibres V and U. The first quotient is locally split because an L-torsor is a tuple of frames of vector bundles, trivialized on their finite algebraic frame charts; for the second quotient the same fact holds directly. The spaces and their fibrations are algebraic, separated and finite type. Restricted to L, U is still a free action because L embeds in G; U has precisely the same ordinary cohomology gap as before. The acyclic-fibre lemma therefore gives the bounded-Hom comparisons on both projections. To see their coefficient identification, pull back to the common principal L-bundle Y x U x V. Both pullbacks are the given coefficient on Y; their descent data are identical L-actions. The locally split Cech descent theorem gives the canonical comparison. On a triple product both identifications are the identity on that same principal bundle, so the cocycle follows. This explicitly verifies the extra model hypotheses; it does not infer stabilization from freeness.

The projections from R are smooth of relative dimensions dim V and dim U. Their smooth BM pullbacks shift by twice those dimensions. The intrinsic index of [F2] on the first quotient is i+2 dim U, on the second i+2 dim V, and on R it is i+2 dim U+2 dim V. Thus the comparison has intrinsic degree zero. The same principal-bundle identity shows compatibility with external products and every equivariant morphism of Y. Proper maps remain proper on the associated quotients; smooth maps remain smooth, and ordinary base change identifies their operations on the common model. The **intrinsic quotient-stack Borel–Moore grading** of this presentation is
$$\mathbb H_i([X/G];\mathbb Q)=H_{i+2g}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;\mathbb Q).$$
The group on the right has exactly the variety dualizing normalization of the cited supplier, $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$. Equivalently, for a sufficiently acyclic free general linear frame space $U$ of dimension $t$, the group is the stable value $H_{i+2t}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;\mathbb Q)$ in each fixed degree. There is no one finite approximation asserted to compute all degrees.

The proper p:E->M_d is represented, using E=[S/G], by the G-equivariant proper incidence map S->X_d. For a finite block flag, P/L has the strictly upper block unipotent coordinates. In particular successive diagonal-forgetting smooth maps compose with exactly this orientation and degree. This proves the flag composition rule used below, rather than assuming it for q.

Here are details ensuring that finite-stage proper/smooth base change and pasting give the interface needed for CoHA. In a 2-Cartesian square of these particular quotient stacks with a representable proper map f and a smooth block-forgetting map q, first choose a free frame cover C_N->C of the common target, with auxiliary dimension t. Since f is representable, A_N=A x_C C_N is a separated finite-type variety and A_N->C_N is proper. Use the induced incidence description to see it as the closed subvariety of the relative flag bundle; no additional source frame is adjoined to that proper arrow. If B->C is nonrepresentable, choose B's adapted-frame presentation and a free frame space of dimension w for its total GL product. Its associated principal-group quotient B_N over C_N is a separated finite-type variety. This follows directly from the upper-block vector-bundle chart over flags in [F2]; after choosing target frames, its map to C_N has fibre (A^e x U)/U_unip. The action is free on the frame factor. Local P-frame sections identify this quotient with an affine bundle over the corresponding frame quotient, so B_N->C_N is smooth of dimension r+w, where r=e-u. Put D_N = A_N x_{C_N} B_N. This is now an actual Cartesian square of varieties; D_N->B_N is proper and D_N->A_N is smooth of dimension r+w. Its four maps are the finite representatives of the original square. Thus the ordinary smooth shift 2(r+w) becomes 2r after the intrinsic normalization of [F2], while both proper shifts remain zero. Ordinary coherent proper/smooth base change applies, so q^! f_* = f'_* (q')^! (4) in the intrinsic groups. The map called q^! here is (3): add the Levi frame as well and compare on their product. On the common adapted-frame principal bundle both maps are the same vector-bundle orientation, with the u-dimensional affine-bundle orientation inverted. The faithful bounded-Hom comparison in [F2] identifies them before passing to groups.

This also proves that these constructions do not depend on cover or presentation. Any two finite choices are compared by their product; on that product the maps are ordinary unit/counit traces and positive complex smooth orientations, and the comparisons are natural in these maps. For a fixed finite collection of maps or equations, choose all frame gaps greater than the finitely many bounded-Hom comparison bounds of their inputs, outputs, units, counits and orientation maps. All objects descend from bounded constructible coefficients on the fixed finite presentation varieties. Faithfulness then reflects the finite-stage equality. One does not choose one N for every degree. This realizes all corners of the pasted diagram as ordinary Cartesian squares simultaneously. The ordinary six-functor theorem says their exchange maps paste: expanding them as adjunction mates reduces the equation to the composition of units/counits and the triangle identities. The product-resolution comparisons preserve those units and counits by their common principal-bundle identity. $N_i\ge n_i+1$ put

   pullback induces an isomorphism

   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;

The identity and cocycle equations are the equations of the inverse-image maps of the same support triangles, so these are actual Cartesian action-nerve coefficients, not unrelated equivariance isomorphisms. Constructibility and boundedness follow from [F2], and normalized equivariant duality [F5] gives $K$ as stated. Angular continuation commutes with every descent map, hence induces the specified monodromy on both coefficients.

Let a free frame $U$ have dimension $t$, put $X_U=X\times_GU$, and let $\Phi_U=V_{f_U}\mathbb Q_{X_U}$. Pulling back to $X\times U$ identifies this with the pullback of $\Phi$ by smooth commutation; the locally split descent of [F3]–[F4] identifies the coefficients downstairs. The representative of the intrinsic $K$ is $D_{X_U}\Phi_U[-2t]$: normalized equivariant duality removes $2(t-g)$ and the further intrinsic shift removes $2g$. Its degree-$(-n)$ cohomology is therefore $H^{-n-2t}(X_U,D\Phi_U)$. This is the critical analogue of the intrinsic index $n+2t$, and for standard coefficients it equals $H_{n+2g}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;\Phi)$ in the original variety-normalized convention; here $H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;\Phi)$ abbreviates $H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G\otimes\Phi)$, which equals the dual-coefficient formula for these standard constant-input cycles by [F2].

The unshifted coefficient $\Phi$ on the fixed presentation has bounded amplitude by [F2]. Its pullbacks to frame factors have the same amplitude. On a local product frame chart the unit comparison is the fixed coefficient complex tensored with the fibre cochain complex; [F4]'s Stiefel gap tends to infinity, so its unit cone has lower bound tending to infinity after that fixed finite width. Thus every fixed-degree Hom and group comparison stabilizes. The normalized dual representative in step 2.1 has the same fixed downstairs bounds after removing the stated auxiliary shift; no bound on the unnormalized dual of growing-dimensional varieties is presumed. On a common product frame bundle both coefficient identifications are the identity on the same pullback from $X$, so they preserve morphisms, operations, monodromy and the triple-product cocycle. This checks the actual hypotheses for [F4] on these vanishing-cycle coefficients.

On $\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}$, [F1] identifies the function with $f_{\mathbf a}\boxplus f_{\mathbf b}$. Smooth commutation and the actual TS isomorphism [F2] therefore identify its intrinsic coefficient $\Psi_E$ with $q^*(\Phi_{\mathbf a,z_1}\boxtimes\Phi_{\mathbf b,z_2})$ on the indicated value-pair summand. In the induced smooth variety presentation of [F3], invariant-flag forgetting is proper. Apply $V$ to its unit $\mathbb Q\to Rp_*\mathbb Q$ and use proper commutation [F2]; this constructs $\Phi_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z}\to Rp_*\Psi_E$. Its dual is $Rp_*D\Psi_E\to D\Phi_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z}$. All fixed-group and auxiliary shifts are the same on the two corners of this proper map, so it has intrinsic degree zero. No closed-restriction isomorphism or integral-identity inverse is used.

For the smooth map use exactly the factorization of [F3]: $[Y/L]\xrightarrow{r}[Y/P]\xrightarrow{q}[Z/L]$, with $r$ an affine fibration of rank $u$ and $qr=v$ a vector-bundle projection of rank $e$. The intrinsic vanishing-cycle coefficient upstairs is the pullback along each such smooth map by [F2]. Duality and positive orientation give the ordinary smooth shifts $2u$ and $2e$, and homotopy invariance [F2] makes $r^!$ an isomorphism. Define $q^!=(r^!)^{-1}v^!$. Its shift is $2(e-u)=-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, and the dual coefficient on the extension stack is exactly $q^*(K_{\mathbf a,z_1}\boxtimes K_{\mathbf b,z_2})[2r]$. This is the required generic smooth identification.

By [F6] only finitely many critical values occur in each dimension. At a point where $df\ne0$, the holomorphic submersion product has zero half-space relative complex, so $V_{f-z}\mathbb Q$ is supported on $\operatorname{Crit}(f)\cap f^{-1}(z)$. For a sum of two smooth functions, its critical locus is the product of their critical loci. The total-value-$z$ support therefore splits into finitely many disjoint closed pieces with values $(z_1,z_2)$ and $z_1+z_2=z$; each piece is also open relative to that support. Closed-support localization gives the canonical direct-sum decomposition. Translating each function by its value and applying TS [F2] on every piece proves exactly the all-values identification of step 4.1. Thus nonzero critical values and nonhomogeneous potentials introduce no omitted summand or completion.

Proper coefficient maps compose because the unit of a composite is the composite of units; smooth base change sends that unit to the unit in the pulled-back diagram. The proper/smooth comparisons of [F2] consequently identify the two resulting coefficient maps. The parent flag construction [F3] realizes the relevant Cartesian diagrams on common finite models, and [F2]'s support-product naturality gives their TS and external-product compatibility. On a three-step flag both TS composites are the coefficient map for the same sum of three diagonal trace functions; positive complex orientations concatenate without a sign because their real degrees are even. The affine-fibration inverse comparisons have the same identities since they invert actual natural isomorphisms. Faithfulness [F4] and step 3.1 reflect these identities from a sufficiently large common model. This proves all composition, base-change, flag-pasting and monodromy coherence demanded by the generic datum.

In dimension zero $f=0$ and $V_0\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q$ by [F2]; the endpoint correspondences are identities, so their coefficient maps and orientations are identities. The group acts by change of basis:
$(g\cdot X)_h=g_jX_hg_i^{-1}$. The **representation stack**
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)/G_{\mathbf d}]$
is the quotient stack: over a scheme $T$, its objects are left

derivations.claim: A one-loop representation of dimension one is a scalar, and change of basis by $\operatorname{GL}_1$ fixes it because conjugation by a scalar is trivial. A dimension-two representation is a $2\times2$ matrix with conjugation action. Preserving a chosen line makes the matrix upper triangular in an adapted basis, as displayed.

For this quiver the off-diagonal rank is $e=1$ and the unipotent vertex-block rank is $u=1$; hence $q$ has relative stack dimension $e-u=0$, agreeing with $-\chi_Q(1,1)=0$. For the splitting change represented by $t\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$, the change-of-basis matrix $g_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ acts by $A\mapsto g_tAg_t^{-1}$, sending $c$ to $c+(\mu-\lambda)t$. The fiber of $p$ at a scalar matrix $\lambda I$ is all of $\mathbb P^1$, so it is positive-dimensional. For a diagonal matrix with distinct eigenvalues, an invariant line must be an eigenspace, giving exactly two points. For a non-scalar Jordan matrix $\lambda I+N$ with $N^2=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}N=1$, an invariant line is $N$-stable; the nilpotent map induced on a one-dimensional line is zero, so the line lies in $\ker N$, which is the unique invariant line.
